newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks firm after Greenspan Senate testimony.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks firm after Greenspan Senate testimony.

text.p: Wall Street shares steadied below session highs by midday Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan wrapped up the second leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony with remarks to the Senate.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up about 40 points, or 0.50 percent, at 8102, below an intraday high of 8148.

The average surged shortly after the open, extending robust gains struck Tuesday after Greenspan's upbeat remarks on the economy to the House. It retreated not long after a flurry of comments from key members of the central bank.
The Nasdaq composite, up about six points at 1570, also weakened from its opening levels.
The long bond was up 4/32 at a 6.41 percent yield.

"In the morning, we saw follow-through from the euphoria which swept markets yesterday," Hugh Johson, chief investment officer of First Albany, said. "Now, even though the stock market is up and the bond market is stable, we are seeing a bit of profit-taking and sobriety creeping into the equation."
Stocks and bonds, which had scrambled higher on Tuesday after Greenspan's testimony, digested more comments from the Fed chief and Fed Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin on Wednesday.

"We have had quite a rollercoaster ride this morning," Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division, said. "We are getting whipsawed by perceptions around Greenspan's testimony before the Senate."

Greenspan delivered the same prepared text to the Senate. He also told the Senate Banking Committee that while U.S. prices have come down, he saw no signs that the economy was about to enter a period of deflation.
Rivlin, in her prepared testimony to the House, warned of the risk of higher U.S. inflation and said it was a "tough call" to decide if the Fed needed to raise rates further.
She also told the House Banking Committee that the dollar "may not get much stronger." The dollar eased from highs, trading at 1.8288/98 marks.
Profit-taking helped push stocks from highs, traders said.

"Greenspan's comments yesterday sent the market back into the stratosphere," Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co, said. "There comes an inevitable point where people see an interim top and take advantage of it to sell. That's natural, even helpful."
Solid corporate earnings results underpinned the broader equity markets, analysts said.

Shares of computer networking company Bay Networks Inc rose 3-4/16 to 32-9/16. Late Tuesday, Bay reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $0.15 per share, before a charge, compared with $0.28 per share in the year-ago quarter.

Boeing Co stock gained 2-14/16 in active trade. The European Commission gave its blessing to Boeing's planned $15 billion merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp after wringing concessions from the Seattle-based aircraft company.
Flowserve Corp jumped 12-1/4 to 36-1/8 in its debut on the New York Stock Exchange.
Shares of Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing Co slipped 1-9/16 to 98-3/4. The company reported second-quarter earnings of $1.01 per share compared with $0.91 per share in the year-ago quarter.
